entities.summary:
Bartolomeo di Breganze (born unknown, died 1270) was a prominent Italian Dominican friar and bishop who played a pivotal role in the Catholic Church's efforts to combat heresy during the medieval period. As the Bishop of Breganze, he was instrumental in leading the Church's response to the Cathars, a Christian dualist movement that threatened the unity of Christendom.

Di Breganze's legacy extends beyond his own time and place, as he contributed to the development of the Inquisition, an institution that would shape Western Christianity for centuries to come. His involvement in the Church's efforts to suppress heresy also had significant repercussions for the relationship between the Catholic Church and secular powers.

Despite the controversies surrounding his legacy, di Breganze remains a fascinating figure whose life and work offer valuable insights into the complex web of power and faith that defined medieval Europe.
